Facts relevant for disposal of the rule, in short, are that opposite party no.1 herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit no. 5 of 1994 for partition and khas possession of suit land claiming that she purchased the suit schedule land from defendant no.1. Suit was decreed in preliminary form which was also upheld by this Division. This petitioner, defendant no.2 of the Title Suit, filed an application for pre-emption under Section 4 of the Partition Act. contending inter alia that defendant no.9 of the suit is his aunt and he purchased share of his aunt and got delivery of possession; opposite party decree holder is an stranger in the suit land; this petitioner has been living with his family on 1/2 sataks of the suit land by erecting houses therein; suit land is an ejmali homestead and as such the petitioner being co-sharer filed instant miscellaneous case to purchase portion of ejmali property transferred to the plaintiff-opposite party no.1. 

 10. Admittedly, this petitioner contested the suit as defendant no.2 in Title Suit No.5 of 1994 preferred by the opposite party no. I as plaintiff seeking partition and khas possession in the suit land. Said suit decreed in preliminary form on 07.06.1998 in favour of the opposite party no. 1 and the decree was upheld by this Division. Ultimately, said preliminary decree was ended up in the form of final decree.
